summary: Evaluation of SEG-00001 reveals the progressive evolution of the canonical Agents.md specification across three commits. The specification evolved from a placeholder to an initial 8-step pipeline (Steps 0-7 with a 31-test schema), and subsequently into a supervisory-gated architecture featuring 14 documented Failure Examples, recursive supervisory gates, structured Step 3 semantic decomposition with TSR testing loops, and a consolidated Step 4 failure-first reporting model.

facts.statement: Commit 20e1fc8 initialized ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/Agents.md with a placeholder string.

Commit ef665db introduced an 8-step procedure (Steps 0 through 7) including return schema persistence, verbatim requirement extraction, a 31-test schema (tests 2-32), Step 3 clause/modifier decomposition with Step3_TSR evaluation loop, completion evidence rules, and a 31-category unrequested action inventory.

Commit 58b6756 added 14 Failure Examples with U/A/E fields, added uniform supervisory_gate schemas requiring key-for-key evaluative mirrors and PASS/FAIL gates to Steps 0-4, restructured Step 3 and Test_Schema into JSON-native format, consolidated failure-first and incomplete reporting into Step 4, and removed the standalone Steps 5, 6, and 7 sections from the file.

interpretations.statement: Commit 58b6756 supersedes the linear step definitions of Steps 4-7 from commit ef665db by integrating failure-first reporting and partial-action verification into Step 4, governed by per-step supervisory gates.
interpretations.rationale: The diff explicitly deleted the standalone text for Steps 5-7 while adding corresponding structured reporting requirements (such as 'Report failure first' and evidence capture) directly into Step 4.

interpretations.statement: The supervisory gate specification creates a strict precondition requiring every returned execution schema to be mirrored and evaluated before proceeding to any subsequent execution step.
interpretations.rationale: All supervisory gate definitions stipulate that gate_result must be PASS before the next execution step may begin, supported by granular key-by-key mirrors and explicit failure tracking linked to Failure Examples.

truth_decisions.decision: Steps 5 through 7 as independent top-level procedure blocks are superseded, with their core reporting and verification constraints partially subsumed into Step 4.
The supervisory gate mechanism and Failure Example taxonomy represent active surviving requirements for agent supervision as of commit 58b6756.

requirement_candidates.name: Start-of-Turn Record and Return Schema
requirement_candidates.description: Initialize a start-of-turn record with verbatim user request, ISO 8601 timestamp, completion booleans, and a unique nonce, persisted to storage and UI.

requirement_candidates.name: Request Preservation and Nonce Matching
requirement_candidates.description: Preserve request exactly as received; UI and persistent records must share the identical request and nonce.

requirement_candidates.name: Verbatim Requirement Extraction
requirement_candidates.description: Extract exclusively user-stated requirements preserved verbatim to ensure full traceability.

requirement_candidates.name: Supervisory Gate Evaluation
requirement_candidates.description: Execute a recursive key-for-key evaluative mirror and step-level evaluation with PASS/FAIL gate blocking subsequent step execution on FAIL.

requirement_candidates.name: Semantic Decomposition and TSR Testing Loop
requirement_candidates.description: Decompose user instruction U into clauses, perform recursive modifier analysis, synthesize plan P and UI output, test against Step3_TSR test suite, and loop back to substep A upon any test match.

requirement_candidates.name: Failure-First Ordered Reporting
requirement_candidates.description: Report all failed actions first with granular evidence, followed by partial/incomplete actions with remaining work, before reporting completed actions.

requirement_candidates.name: Standalone 31-Category Action Inventory
requirement_candidates.description: Maintain standalone Step 7 schema covering 31 explicit categories of agent action authorization checks.

implementation_findings.statement: The supervisory gate structure is fully documented in Agents.md markdown patches, but this segment provides no executable code or deterministic runtime harness to confirm active enforcement.

contradictions.description: Failure Example 14 highlights an inherent status contradiction ('didReadback = true, but didReadback = false') where an agent asserted operation completion while acknowledging that verification comparison had been skipped.

unresolved.description: Whether the supervisory gate evaluation and Step3_TSR evaluation loop are executed via an external orchestrator, LLM prompt chaining, or custom application logic cannot be determined from the Agents.md patch log alone.
